html:
SMTO-SKL-0061 — Microsoft 365 files can only be moved inside a conversation

GUID: 7fb1a8e1-803d-51e9-8bf6-9467bae29a32
Slug: microsoft365-artifact-context-required
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • To download or upload Outlook attachments or OneDrive files, SMTO keeps them inside a conversation. This request ran somewhere without one, so SMTO stopped before moving any file.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open SMTO's main conversation view, start or open a conversation, and type your request there, for example "download the attachment from Anna's last email". Files moved to or from Microsoft 365 are kept with a conversation, so the request has to come from one.
  2. For an upload or an email attachment, first add the file to that same conversation with Add files to conversation. SMTO only sends files that belong to the conversation you are in.
  3. If you already asked from a normal conversation, start a new conversation and ask there once more. A new conversation gets its own file area, so this shows whether only the first one was set up wrongly.

What success looks like

  • The downloaded file appears under Artifacts in the conversation, or SMTO confirms the upload or attachment by name.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Say where you made the request (a conversation, a Workflow or somewhere else) and that a new conversation didn't help.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Microsoft 365 file or attachment transfer was attempted without an artifact registry or without a current run and conversation scope in the tool context.

What this means

  • File transfer setup lacks an artifact registry or current run/conversation scope. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • File transfer setup lacks an artifact registry or current run/conversation scope.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the artifact context and ownership passed to the transfer.

How to fix it

  • Run the transfer from a native Agent run, where artifacts.runtime.bind places _artifact_store and _artifact_scope (run_id and conversation_id) in the tool context. If a normal conversation run still raises this, the run's artifact workspace binding failed; check the Server log for that run.
  • Run the transfer inside a task with an artifact workspace and conversation ownership.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The transfer runs with the intended active conversation artifact workspace.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
